# Parts of a page and their styles

The parts of a page's tree, or of a component's own tree (`at: { component: <key> }`, inside component.edit for the header, the footer and the layouts): insert, move, remove and copy parts, their words, props, styles, attributes, visibility and audience.

## tree.insert

Insert new nodes (one part and what it holds) as child `index` of a parent node, on a page or in a component's own tree. Use it for a part built from scratch: a text, a picture, a box holding them. For a whole section built from one of the site's components use section.insert or section.addKind; for a saved preset, preset.insert; for one component, instance.insert. Every node of `nodes` hangs from `root`; the motion wholly inside them (`motion`) and their translations (`l10n`) may come with them. Refusals: `op_target` (no such parent, or an index past its children), `not_a_parent` (a text or a picture holds no children), `duplicate_id`, `orphan_node`, `invalid_input`; the tree it leaves is validated, a broken rule refusing with its id (`tree.content-model`: an element that may not hold another; `css.grammar`; `ref.token`).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "wrap", "group".

## tree.remove

Remove a node and everything under it, with its translations and the motion wholly inside it. The timelines and states that name only its nodes go with it, and the waits on that motion (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends); `motion: false` leaves that motion where it is, `waits: false` those waits. For a whole section of a page use section.remove, for one item of a list slot.remove. Refusals: `op_target` (no such node, or the tree's root), `template_node` (a part a repeat or an instance draws: remove the repeat or the instance), `lock.removed` (a locked node or one under it: tree.set_locked unlocks it), `motion.starts_from_wait` (a timeline that stays starts from a wait it would take). Output: `{ took: { timelines, states, locks } }` of the motion it took (`locks`: the gates among its states that held the page's scroll), else null.

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "unwrap".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `motion` | false |  | false: leave the motion that names only its nodes where it is. |
| `waits` | false |  | false: leave the waits on that motion where they are. |

Example inputs:

```json

```

## tree.move

Move a node, with everything under it, to another parent or to another place among its siblings. `index` counts the parent's children once the node has left. To wrap parts in a new box: tree.insert an empty frame where the first part is, then tree.move each part into it (index 0, 1, 2) in one batch; to unwrap, tree.move the box's children out after it, then tree.remove the box. Refusals: `op_target` (no such node or parent, or a node a repeat or an instance holds), `cycle` (the parent is inside the node), `not_a_parent`, `lock.moved` (a locked node keeps its parent).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "wrap", "unwrap", "group", "reorder".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `parent` | string | yes | The id of the frame (or group, vector) it goes in. |
| `index` | integer ≥0 | yes | Its place among that parent's children, counted without it: 0 first. |


## tree.set_props

Set or clear props of a node: its own name, a link's address and target, a picture's file and alt text, an anchor, a surface, a line that fills a width (`fit`). null clears a prop, and the translations of what it held. Its words, style, attributes, visibility and place have their own ops (tree.set_text, tree.set_style, tree.set_attrs, tree.set_visibility, tree.move), its element tree.set_type; `kind` never changes. Refusals: `invalid_input` for one of those fields (`text`, `style`, `children`, `kind`, `hidden`), `invalid_node` for a prop the node's kind does not take; the validator's rules (`link.target`, `media.ref`, `text.fit`).

A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |

## tree.derive_anchors

Give each heading below a node that has no anchor one made from its words, unique in the tree, so a `#` link reaches it. `tags` takes the texts of those elements instead of the headings. The anchors are stored, so a link to one survives a later edit of its words; tree.set_props `anchor` sets one by hand. Output: node id → the anchor given.

## tree.set_locked

Lock a node to its place, or unlock it. A locked node keeps its parent and cannot be removed (later edits that would are refused as `lock.moved` and `lock.removed`); its words, props and style stay editable. Use it for the parts the page's structure needs, such as the frame that holds its sections.

A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |

## tree.set_style

Set or clear CSS declarations of a node in one style scope. `scope` says when they hold: `base` always, `bp:md` while the site's `md` breakpoint holds, `s:hover` while hovered, `mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, parts joined by `|` (`bp:md|s:hover`); the field gives the whole grammar. A value is CSS text, a number or a design token (`{ $token: 'color.text.accent' }`); null clears that property in the scope. To hide a part on some screens only, set `display: none` in a `bp:` or `mq:` scope. A header, footer or component part is styled in its component's tree (`at: { component }`), one instance alone with instance.override. Refusals: the site's guidelines (`guideline.fixed`; `guideline.choice`: the property takes one of the tokens discovery lists), the validator's (`css.grammar`, `ref.token` for an unknown token, `scope.known` for an unknown breakpoint, state or part, `scope.selector`). A text colour that fails AA on its ground is corrected in the same step by the contrast check, or refused.

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "colour", "color", "spacing", "padding", "margin", "css", "mobile", "phone", "responsive".

|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `scope` | string (max 300) | yes | When a style holds: `base` (always), or parts joined by `\|`, all of which hold (`bp:md\|s:hover`). Each part is `<prefix>:<value>`: `bp:<name>` from a breakpoint of the site up (mobile first; names such as sm, md, lg, xl are in the tokens read); `mq:<media query>` (`mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `mq:(hover: none)`); `cq:<container query>`; `s:<state>` the node's own state (`s:hover`, `s:focus-visible`, `s:active`, `s:current`, `s:open`, `s:checked`, `s:empty`, `s:loaded`, `s:playing`), a state the page sets on nodes (`s:scene-active`, `s:step=2`), or selector terms (`s:::after`, `s::not([href])`, `s:[aria-expanded="true"]`); `a:<state>` the same state held by an ancestor (`a:hover`: the link or button around it is hovered); `pg:<state>=<value>` a page state, any of several values (`pg:menu=open`, `pg:menu=closed,open`); `p:<part>` a named part of the widget it is (`p:track`); `sub:<subset>` the items of a repeat subset; `st:enter` the style it starts from when it first shows; `sp:word` or `sp:char` each word or letter of a split text; `t:<selector>` its descendants (`t: a`, `t:> li`); `th:<theme>` where that theme applies; `fmt:<format>` when drawn in that output format. |

## tree.set_audience

Show a node only to the site's signed-in members, only to guests, or to every visitor again (`audience: null`). With `who: members`, `roles` narrows it to members holding one of those member roles. A whole page's access is page.setAccess; this is for a part of a page, or of the header and footer (inside component.edit of their definition). Refused: `audience.role` (a member role the site does not have: memberRole.create adds one), `op_target` (no such node, or the tree's root, which every visitor gets).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "hide", "private".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `audience` | { who: "members", roles?: string (max 40)[] (≤20) } \| { who: "guests" } \| null | yes | { who: "members", roles?: member role keys } or { who: "guests" }; null: every visitor. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"q7ez12qr","audience":{"who":"members","roles":["clienti"]}}
```
```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"q7ez12qr","audience":null}
```

## tree.set_type

Change the HTML element a frame, a text or a media node renders as: a heading's level, a box made a section or a link, a video made audio. Other kinds are refused (`invalid_input`), an element the kind does not take too (`invalid_node`); the validator refuses one its place forbids (`tree.content-model`).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `as` | string (max 20) | yes | The element: a frame takes div, section, article, header, footer, nav, a, button, ul, ol, li and more; a text p, h1 to h6, span, blockquote and more; a media video or audio. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"title001","as":"h2"}
```
```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"card0001","as":"section"}
```

## tree.set_text

Set the words a text node shows in the site's main language: plain words (`text`) or runs with marks (`runs`: bold, italic, links, line breaks), exactly one of the two. Other languages are translation.set's; when a text goes from plain words to runs or back, its translations follow it. In a repeat's template a text may read the item (`{ $item: 'title' }`), in a component a prop (`{ $prop: 'title' }`). Refused for a node that is not a text (`invalid_input`); the validator checks the runs (`text.runs`).

- **op**; class `content` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "heading", "headline", "title", "text", "words".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `text` | string (max 4000) \| number \| { $token: string } \| { $cell: string } \| { $prop: string } \| { $item: string } \| { $state: string } \| { $bind: string (max 80), template?: string (min 1, max 80), fallback?: string (max 200), pair?: { foreground: string (min 3, max 120), background: string (min 3, max 120), theme?: string (… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) |  | Plain words, or a value that reads them: `{ $item: 'title' }`, `{ $bind: 'page.title' }`, `{ $prop: 'title' }`. |
| `runs` | (string (min 1, max 100000) \| { t: string (min 1, max 100000), m?: ("strong" \| "em" \| "u" \| "s" \| "mark" \| "sub" \| "sup" \| "code" \| "kbd" \| { a: { target: "_blank", … } } \| { span: … })[] (≤11) } \| { br: true })[] (≤2000) |  | The words as runs: a string; `{ t: 'words', m: ['strong'] }` with marks (strong, em, u, s, mark, sub, sup, code, kbd, `{ a: { href: '/contatti' } }`, `{ span: { lang: 'en' } }`); `{ br: true }` for a line break. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"title001","text":"Diamo forma alla luce"}
```
```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"intro001","runs":["Studio di architettura a Roma. ",{"t":"Scrivici","m":[{"a":{"href":"/contatti"}}]},{"br":true},{"t":"Dal 1998","m":["strong"]}]}
```

## tree.set_theme

Set or clear the theme of a node and everything under it: one of the site's themes, such as its dark one, which its tokens follow there. Use it to put a section or a card in another theme; `theme: null` clears it, and the node takes the theme around it. Refused: `theme.known` (the site has no such theme, or a token set it reads is missing), `op_target` (no such node).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "dark".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `theme` | string (min 1, max 64) \| null | yes | A theme key of the site (site_context lists its themes, such as dark); null: the node takes the theme around it. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"acceuvhm","theme":"dark"}
```
```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"acceuvhm","theme":null}
```

## tree.set_mixins

Set or clear the mixins a node takes: named styles of the site (mixin.set), in order, the later winning, below the node's own style. `mixins: null` clears them. Refused: `mixin.known` (a mixin the site does not have, or one listed twice), `op_target` (no such node).

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet. |
| `mixins` | string (min 1, max 64)[] (≤8) \| null | yes | Mixin keys of the site, in order (the later wins); null clears the list. |

Example input:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"5zfqbql3","mixins":["didascalia"]}
```

## tree.duplicate

Copy a part and everything under it right after itself, under fresh ids, with the motion wholly inside it. Use it for a part inside a section or a card (a paragraph, a picture, a column); copy a whole section with section.insert from a page, and a list's item with slot.add. The copy is named `name` when given; an anchor is not copied; motion that also reaches outside the part stays behind, named in a `motion.left_behind` finding (`motion: false` copies none). Refused: `duplicate.not_a_part` (the tree's root, or a part a list or a repeat holds; for a list's item the sentence names the slot.add with `source: { copy }` that copies it), `op_target` (no such node). Output: { root } of the copy.

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | The part to copy: a node of the tree `at` names, whose parent is a frame, group or vector (node/<pageId>?node= reads it). |
| `name` | string (min 1, max 80) |  | The copy's own name in Structure; absent: the name the part has. |
| `motion` | false |  | false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part. |

Example input:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"5zfqbql3","name":"Riga in evidenza, seconda"}
```
